correctness.rationale: For center O outside/on unit disk, the visible circle directions occupy ≤π radians and leave an angular gap ≥π of zero arclength mass. Positive 1/(3k) mass in each basic sector forces the gap into at most two consecutive sectors; the containing convex (k+1)-wedge (k≥2) then has angle >π, contradiction. For interior O, radial projection of the support circle to directions about O preserves cyclic order, hence 1/n arclength per basic sector means intercepts P_j at equally spaced angles φ+2πj/n. For m=k+1, Δ=2πm/n≤π and sin(Δ/2)>0. det(P_j−O,P_{j+m}−O)=2 sin(Δ/2)[cos(Δ/2)−O·u_j] directly equates wedge convexity with one half-plane. The n equally spaced normals give a regular polygon with inradius c=cos(π(k+1)/(3k)); k=2 has c=0 and collapses to origin, k≥3 has circumradius c/cos(π/(3k))=(1/2)−(√3/2)tan(π/(3k))<1/2. Reversible construction, standard area n c²tan(π/n), rotating union/intersection and limit π/4 complete proof. Independently tested determinant for k=2..119 and phase/radius identities; finite checks not proof.
residual_risks: Proof concerns circle arclength measure only, not general smooth radial densities.

value.rationale: The circle is a canonical singular planar mass satisfying the source’s no-mass-on-lines condition. The complete center/phase moduli classification is a motivated exact solution of the new (3k,k+1) convex-spiral existence regime, not merely one example. It identifies rigid k=2, the positive-area regular center polygons for k≥3, two distinct radial feasibility thresholds and quantitative convergence to a radius-1/2 disk. These are independently useful precise facts for partition geometry even absent a general-mass theorem.
residual_risks: The result does not characterize any other planar mass or nonspiral partition and has a focal-literature access risk.

final_claim: For normalized circular arclength mass and k≥2, every convex (3k,k+1)-spiral equicovering has regular 3k-gon boundary intercepts, and its feasible centers at fixed intercept phase form the exact regular center polygon C_{k,φ}={O:O·u_j≤cos(π(k+1)/(3k)) for all j}; C_{2,φ}={0}, other polygons have the stated inradius, circumradius, area and radial phase-union/intersection.
limitations: Only normalized arclength on a circle, exact convex spiral regime (n,m)=(3k,k+1).
